figures.caption: Figure 1: Brain–DNN alignment as approximate naturality (motivational concept diagram). Left: the World Model W parameterizes which stimulus change r : s → s′ is tested; the translators η : B → M and η′ : M → B connect the two sides. Right: the naturality square (the analogous square is also asked of η′). This is the motivational categorical reading; in practice FB(r), FM (r) are not estimated as endomorphisms of B,M but realized at first order via the proxy chain FW ,ΦB ,ΦM (Fig. 2); FB , FM are not enforced to be strict functors (App. A1).

Figure 2: Dual-triangle decomposition of NVS. Each world morphism ∆W has two paths to a target space. Left: direct ΦM (∆W ) vs. brain-mediated η(ΦB(∆W )). Right: direct ΦB(∆W ) vs. DNN-mediated η′(ΦM (∆W )). NVS is the symmetric mean of the two per-direction permutation-normalized residuals (§3); used identically in the synthetic PoC and the empirical fMRI study.

Table 2: Per-axis NVSa for the 6 main scalar axes: per-FW pooled mean and best cell. The first three numeric columns give the 5-subject mean across the 3DNN× 5ROI× 8 layer cells for each (FW , axis), reported as µ±σ with σ the across-5-subjects SD of the pooled per-subject mean. The last column gives the cell minimizing the 5-subject mean across all 9 (FW ,DNN) blocks × 5ROI × 8 layer. A = AlexNet, R = ResNet, V = ViT-B. Entries marked † are proxy-axis combinations that fail the proxy-viability criterion (R2 ≤ 0 in held-out CAV readout); they are retained for transparency and should not be interpreted as valid tests of that morphism family for that proxy.

Figure 3: 5-subject mean NVSa (6 scalar-axis rows) and NVSfull (full-FW row, bottom) × 3 FW × 3 vision DNNs. Each submap is a 5ROI× 8 layer heatmap, ROI horizontal (V1→HVC), layer vertical (L1→L8). Color: deep blue = stronger preservation, white = permutation null (1.0), red = above null. A/R/V = AlexNet/ResNet/ViT-B. The axis-resolved rows show the hierarchy crossover (low-level axes → V1×shallow; semantic axes → HVC×deep), absent in the diffuse full-FW row. Per-subject heatmaps: Fig. A2; statistical crossover: Tab. A2. Submaps failing the CAV viability screen are marked † (in the heatmap and in the corresponding tables) and should not be read as valid tests.

Table 3: Full-vector NVSfull for each (FW ,DNN) combination. Each numeric entry is µ± σ where µ is the 5-subject mean over the relevant ROI×layer cells and σ is the across-5-subjects SD of that pooled per-subject mean. The pooled-mean column averages over all 5ROI × 8 layer cells for that FW , and the best-cell column reports the single (ROI, layer, DNN) cell minimizing the 5-subject mean for that FW , with σ the across-5-subjects SD of that best cell. A = AlexNet, R = ResNet, V = ViT-B. This table gives the unrestricted whole-space comparison as background to the per-axis analyses above. (NVS reading convention: lower is better, 1.0 is chance; §A3 Evaluation.)
